risk_description: Data consistency corruption due to 'Last Write Wins' conflict resolution strategy in offline-first synchronization between Isar local DB and Aurora backend.
root_cause: The architectural decision to use simple 'Last Write Wins' logic may result in data loss if a user modifies the same record (e.g., reading session) on multiple devices while offline.
mitigation_strategy: Implement a 'Delta Sync' pattern sending only changed fields rather than full entities. Enforce strict UTC timestamping on client mutations. Develop a specific conflict resolution matrix for critical entities.
contingency_plan: Implement a server-side audit log of overwritten data to allow manual restoration if user reports data loss. Fallback to 'Server Wins' for critical financial/subscription data.
monitoring_trigger: Detection of sync request timestamps older than the current server record timestamp exceeding 5% of total sync traffic.

risk_description: Subscription state mismatch caused by failures or delays in processing server-to-server webhooks from Apple App Store and Google Play Store.
root_cause: Dependency on external asynchronous webhooks for Premium status updates combined with potential network jitter or downtime in the webhook processing lambda/endpoint.
mitigation_strategy: Implement an idempotent webhook processing queue using Amazon SQS with DLQ. Design the client to validate receipts locally with the backend immediately upon purchase completion as a primary confirmation.
contingency_plan: Develop a nightly reconciliation job (cron) that queries Apple/Google APIs for all active subscriptions to self-heal state mismatches.
monitoring_trigger: CloudWatch alarm for SQS Dead Letter Queue depth > 0 for the webhook processing queue.

risk_description: Excessive operational costs and latency in the AI RAG pipeline due to unoptimized OpenSearch vector queries and high-frequency OpenAI API calls.
root_cause: Premium users with unlimited AI suggestion access (US-091) combined with per-token pricing models and complex k-NN search queries.
mitigation_strategy: Implement aggressive semantic caching using Redis to serve repeated similar queries. Enforce strict rate limiting per user on the backend. Optimize vector dimensions.
contingency_plan: Downgrade model from GPT-4 to GPT-3.5-Turbo or a smaller embedding model if costs exceed monthly budget thresholds.
monitoring_trigger: Daily cost forecast exceeding 110% of budget in AWS Cost Explorer or OpenAI usage dashboard.

risk_description: Mobile application UI jank (dropped frames) during heavy data processing due to blocking the main thread with Isar DB queries or JSON parsing.
root_cause: Flutter runs Dart code on a single UI thread by default. Heavy local database operations (e.g., syncing 1000s of records) can freeze the UI if not explicitly offloaded.
mitigation_strategy: Mandate the use of Flutter `compute()` or `Isolates` for all data parsing and heavy database batch operations. Establish a performance budget for frame build times.
contingency_plan: Implement pagination/infinite scrolling for all list views to limit the data processed at any one time.
monitoring_trigger: Sentry reporting 'App Not Responding' (ANR) events or frame build times > 16ms in performance profiling.

risk_description: Core library search functionality failure due to Google Books API rate limiting or strict quotas.
root_cause: The application relies heavily on a third-party public API for book metadata which has strict usage quotas.
mitigation_strategy: Implement the Backend Proxy (WI-LIB-001) with aggressive caching policies. Use multiple API keys if compliant with TOS. Implement a 'Manual Entry' fallback (US-055).
contingency_plan: Switch to Open Library API as a secondary provider if Google Books becomes unreliable or cost-prohibitive.
monitoring_trigger: Http 429 (Too Many Requests) error rate from Google Books Proxy exceeding 1%.

risk_description: Data loss or app crashes on mobile clients due to improper handling of Isar database schema migrations during app updates.
root_cause: NoSQL local databases on mobile require strict migration paths when data models change between app versions.
mitigation_strategy: Establish a strict schema versioning protocol. Write automated migration tests for every schema change. Use feature flags to roll out schema changes cautiously.
contingency_plan: Implement a 'nuke and sync' recovery option that wipes the local DB and re-downloads fresh data from the server if corruption is detected.
monitoring_trigger: Spike in crash reports (Sentry) referencing `IsarError` or schema mismatch exceptions after a new release.
